newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's top Indian official quits, blasts government.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's top Indian official quits, blasts government.

text.p: Brazil's top Indian affairs official resigned on Wednesday, accusing the government of failing to honour its promises to help indigenous people.

Julio Gaiger, National Indian Foundation (Funai) president since March 1996, said the government had abandoned a programme introduced last year that sought to break with Brazil's traditionally paternal approach to Indian issues.
He also took a swipe at resistance to change among some Indian groups, saying they had grown too dependent on special treatment from "a paternal and authoritarian state."

Gaiger, who speaks several indigenous languages and was once stripped naked to take part in an Indian ceremony, lasted longer as Funai president than most of his predecessors, who usually spent less than a year in the job.

His office was regularly stormed by Indians seeking to press their demands. Several other groups, angry over the government's failure to demarcate their reservations and provide them with basic services, had been calling for him to be fired.
